questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Shikha said, "The heavy rain this week has spoiled all my travel plans."
options_en: Shikha said that the heavy rain that week had spoiled all her travel plans.
Shikha told me that the heavy rain that week had spoiled all her travel plans.
Shikha said that the heavy rain that week has spoiled all her travel plans.
Shikha said that the heavy rain this week had spoiled all her travel plans.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Present Perfect Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'This week' would be changed to 'that week'.

'Has spoiled' would be changed to 'had spoiled'.

'My' would be changed to 'her'.

Since there is no object of the verb 'said' in the sentence in direct speech, 'said' would be changed to 'said that' only.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): Shikha said that the heavy rain that week had spoiled all her travel plans.

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

In China, there once lived a father, his four sons, and three daughters-in-law. His three older sons had married within a few months of each other and all with young women from the same village. Recently, these three new daughters-in-law had been brought into the house. Their new father-in-law's wife had died a few years before and having no mother-in-law with them in their new home, and being lonesome and homesick for their former families, they constantly asked the old man for permission to visit their former village. For you see, those were the days when young women, after they married and moved into the homes of their new husbands, needed permission to leave the household. Annoyed by the continual pleas of his three new daughters-in-law, the old father thought of a way to put an end to it.

He gave the young women permission in this way, saying, "You are always begging me to allow you to go and visit your mothers, and you think I am very hard-hearted for not letting you go. Now you may go, but only upon this condition. When you come back, you must each bring me something that I want. One of you must bring me some fire in paper, the other must bring me some wind in paper, and the third must bring me some music in wind. Unless you promise to bring me this, you are never to ask me to let you go home. And if you go and fail to get these for me, you are never to come back." The old man did not suppose that these conditions would be accepted. Of course, they were hard to understand, much less to fulfil. But the girls were young and thoughtless, and in their anxiety to get away did not consider any of that. So, they promised and made ready with speed. In great glee, they started off on foot to visit their mothers.

Which of the following sentences is TRUE as per the passage?
options_en: All the newlywed women were from the same village.
Two of the daughters-in-law were from one village and the third one was from another village.
All three daughters-in-law were cousins before marriage.
The old man had two wives.
questions.solution_en:
The following sentence from the first paragraph of the given passage states that "His three older sons had married within a few months of each other and all with young women from the same village." Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Other options are incorrect as per the passage.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The letter was wrote / by my sister yesterday / with a new pen.
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the part "The letter was wrote". The sentence is in the passive voice. In passive voice constructions, the past participle form (V3) of the main verb is used with an auxiliary verb (a form of 'to be'). The past participle of "write" is "written," not "wrote" (which is the simple past form, V2). The auxiliary verb 'was' (singular) is correct for the singular subject 'The letter'.

Correct Sentence: The letter was written by my sister yesterday with a new pen.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). The past participle (V3) form is used here.

· Passive Voice: When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. Example: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends.

· Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. 'Was' is an auxiliary verb here.

questions.solution_en:

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said, 'Let us wait for the award'.
options_en: He proposed that they should wait for the award.
He said that he should wait for the award.
He proposed that he should wait for the award.

questions.solution_en:
Option (a) is the correct answer.

"Let" is used to mean "to allow" (request) or "to propose/suggest".

"Let" as a proposal/suggestion:

Rules to follow:

"Said/said to" is changed to "proposed/proposed to" or "suggested/suggested to"

That is added in indirect speech.

"Let" is removed in the indirect speech.

Modal verb "should" is added in indirect speech.

Pronouns are changed accordingly.

Example 1: He said, "Let us go to the amusement park." (Direct Speech)

He suggested that they should go to the amusement park. (Indirect Speech)

Example 2: I said to him, "Let us attend the office party." (Direct Speech)

I proposed to him that we should attend the office party. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

The reporting verb 'said' is changed into 'proposed'.

Inverted commas is removed and 'that' is introduced.

The pronoun 'us' is changed into 'they'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): He proposed that they should wait for the award.

"Peace" is the correct choice. It's a noun that refers to a state of harmony and absence of conflict. It perfectly fits the context of a treaty ending a long-standing conflict between nations.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Some water were given to the dogs after the long day of the outing.
questions.solution_en:
When any of 'some, any, none, all, more / most, is used with an uncountable noun, the verb is singular.

'Water' is an uncountable noun. So, 'were' [plural] should be replaced with 'was' [singular].

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Note:-

Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table' - one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word.

Entire - Means whole or complete. This word doesn't have any emotional connection to "despondent."

Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object).

Bought - had bought

This - that

My - his

Therefore, the correct answer is (c): He said that he had bought that book for his brother.

questions.q_en:
Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options.

A. Recently, an documentary on Cold War was screened. It provided the comprehensive overview of that period.

B. Recently, the documentary on a Cold War was screened. It provided a comprehensive overview of that period.

C. Recently, a documentary on an Cold War was screened. It provided an comprehensive overview of that period.

D. Recently, a documentary on the Cold War was screened. It provided a comprehensive overview of period.
questions.solution_en:
The indefinite article 'a' should be used before 'documentary' because it is introducing an unspecified noun 'documentary'. Similarly, the indefinite article 'a' should also be used before 'comprehensive' because it refers to an unspecified and singular noun, that is, 'overview'. Also, since 'documentary' and 'comprehensive' are not vowel-sounding words, they cannot be preceded by 'an'.

The definite article 'the' should be used before 'Cold War' because it introduces a specific noun 'Cold War'.

No indefinite article is used before 'overview' because it is uncountable in nature.

The sentences A, B, and C depict grammatically incorrect usage of the articles.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer. Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

Similarly, the indefinite article 'a' should also be used before 'comprehensive' because it refers to an unspecified and singular noun, that is, 'overview'. Also, since 'documentary' and 'comprehensive' are not vowel-sounding words, they cannot be preceded by 'an'.

The definite article 'the' should be used before 'Cold War' because it introduces a specific noun 'Cold War'.

No indefinite article is used before 'overview' because it is uncountable in nature.

The sentences A, B, and C depict grammatically incorrect usage of the articles.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer. Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

'Elated' means very happy or excited, 'allude' means to hint or refer to something indirectly, and 'elude' means to escape or avoid.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Rita made ourself some tomato soup.
questions.solution_en:
The blank requires a reflexive pronoun because it reflects Rita and that the action of preparing food is directed towards herself and not anyone else. The only contextually applicable reflexive pronoun is 'herself'. Options b) and c) are incorrect because they are a personal pronoun and a determiner respectively. 'Ourself' is not applicable as the subject is a singular female. Therefore, the correct answer is option d).

Note:

Pronoun: A pronoun is a word that replaces a noun and acts as a substitute for it.

Reflexive Pronouns: These pronouns are used when the subject of the sentence is also the object of the sentence; in other words, these pronouns show that the action done by the subject is directed toward not anyone else but the subject. This is illustrated in the examples below:

Kids enjoyed themselves at the party.

Rakhee made herself some tea.

Personal Pronouns:

The pronouns that are used for three persons, namely, the person speaking, the person spoken to, and the person spoken of, are called personal pronouns.

Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

questions.q_en:

questions.solution_en:

'Sly' means artfully cunning.

'Horrid' means rough and rugged.

'Feeble' means deficient in physical strength.
